tagline: One terrain, spanning golden-hour scrubland to cold misty highland as world state. A from-scratch Three.js engine graded against PS4-native reference frames: builders ship, critics score blind, the single biggest gap comes back. Repeat until the tier is indistinguishable.

systems.name: Scene Foundation
systems.brief: Sky, atmosphere, terrain, lighting, shadows, grade — plus a time-of-day and weather system so one zone spans both reference art directions. The dependency root; every other system renders on top of this.
systems.gap: ROUND 2 LANDED. The corduroy ripple both critics independently traced to macRelief() is gone from every shot. Scatter density is up 3-4x inside the playable bowl, storm now shows real standing water, and backlit scrub genuinely glows gold against the dark hillside — the FFXV money shot works. Not re-scored yet.
systems.next: Held by directive until gameplay systems are running. Re-score after phase 1 functionality is complete.

rubric.name: Lighting & tonemapping
rubric.note: Sky scattering, IBL ambient and colour space all read PS4-tier. Held back by a flat white clipped patch around the sun disc in grazing and dawn.

rubric.name: Shadows & contact
rubric.note: Contact darkening under rocks is convincing (3/4). Killed by R2.2 at 1/4 — a mechanically regular corduroy ripple raked across the midground in 7 of 9 shots.

rubric.name: Terrain & world scale
rubric.note: Layered silhouettes and aerial perspective are genuine strengths (3/4 each). Ground detail at eye height scored 1/4 — the same ripple artifact.

rubric.name: Foliage & density
rubric.note: Weakest section. Backlit translucency 1/4 (scrub reads as flat opaque silhouettes), wind 1/4 (no coherent gust direction), density countable rather than a field.

rubric.name: Post & atmosphere
rubric.note: Per-weather grade praised as genuinely PS4-tier and clearly differentiated. Bloom bleeds into non-HDR sky around the sun.

rubric.name: Time-of-day & weather
rubric.note: Night (3/4) and golden hour (3/4) are authored and hold up. Overcast nearly shapeless (1/4) and storm wetness reads as a colour shift, not water (1/4).

systems.name: Character System
systems.brief: Original humanoid mesh, skeleton, skinning, PBR materials, idle animation. No copyrighted likeness or ripped rig.
systems.gap: HALF-BUILT — the Character builder was killed mid-write by the account spend limit. Its work survived and is committed: a real skinned humanoid with skeleton, outfit, belt and buckle across four modules (build, geom, material, rig). But the portrait shot shows the surface is shredded — heavy mesh artifacts across the whole body, a scribbled face, and detached floating eyeballs. It renders and holds 83-87 fps, so the pipeline is sound; the geometry generation is not finished.
systems.next: Opus builder running: repairing the shredded mesh and skin weights, then re-targeting the design to Oz Macrion per the story canon — anime-styled sculpted hair readable as a silhouette in backlit, sword and flute visible, royal-but-travelling wardrobe. Judged at the hero and portrait poses.

systems.name: Environment, NPCs & Enemies
systems.brief: NPC and enemy characters reusing the player rig, plus props, landmarks and set dressing that make the basin a place rather than terrain.
systems.next: Wave 2. Snagulas (Haiku) reusing the character rig once Oz is repaired, plus combat and enemy AI (Sonnet).

systems.name: Story, Quest & Cinematics
systems.brief: Original Macrion premise, the first major quest, branching dialogue, progression state, and a data-driven cutscene system with spline camera moves.
systems.gap: PARTIALLY BUILT then killed by the spend limit. Surviving and committed: story.js, quest.js, dialogue.js, interaction.js, eventBus.js for game systems, plus cutscene.js and cutscene-data.js for cinematics. None verified end to end.
systems.next: Two builders running: Game Systems (Sonnet) verifying the quest machinery and replacing all placeholder narrative with the real canon — authoring Act 0 (the flute and the Great Head) and Act 0.5 (descent, first Snagulas, Sarah song) as playable quest data. Cinematics (Haiku) verifying cutscene camera authority never soft-locks.

systems.name: Player, Audio & UI
systems.brief: Third-person controller with terrain collision, adaptive synthesized score and ambience, and the HUD overlay. Everything audio is generated in code — no samples, no copyrighted music.
systems.gap: PARTIALLY BUILT then killed by the spend limit. Surviving and committed: six audio modules (synth, score, music, ambience, sfx, audio) all synthesized in code with no samples, plus hud.js/hud.css and the player controller. None verified end to end.
systems.next: Two builders running: Audio (Sonnet) verifying six never-run modules, wiring the explore/alert/combat/boss/resolve music state machine, and composing Sarah motif — the recurring theme that returns at every major beat. HUD (Haiku) verifying zero HUD pixels leak into captures.
